# Cross-Exchange Liquidity Commentary – 2026-07-30

The ranking reveals a clear three-tier structure. Nasdaq 100 and NYSE dominate as leaders, with Nasdaq posting the tightest ILLIQ at 0.0025% per $1M traded and NYSE offering the narrowest AR spread of 0.6530%, though comparable volumes of $424.9M and $203.9M respectively reflect their structural advantage. A mid-pack cluster comprising Tokyo Stock Exchange, Euronext, Hong Kong Stock Exchange, and SIX Swiss Exchange shows more heterogeneous profiles: Tokyo's 3.9700% turnover ratio signals robust local activity despite an ILLIQ cost of 0.0360% per $1M, while Euronext's 0.5495% AR spread ranks among the tightest globally yet its comparable volume of only $15.3M constrains absolute liquidity provision. Korea Exchange and Xetra occupy the lower-middle tier, with Korea Exchange notably diverging—its 1.5659% AR spread and 0.1489% ILLIQ per $1M traded suggest structural friction, though 1.5754% turnover hints at concentrated domestic trading. London Stock Exchange ranks last, combining a 0.0821% ILLIQ cost with the widest 0.7954% AR spread, suggesting execution costs remain elevated despite reasonable turnover. Overall, size and geographic centrality remain primary liquidity drivers.
